about: Hillrock Estate Distillery sits on a 75-acre farm in Ancram, Columbia County, in the Hudson Valley about two hours north of Manhattan, around a restored Federal-style farmhouse from 1806. Jeffrey Baker founded it in 2011 with the late Dave Pickerell, the former Master Distiller of Maker’s Mark, who designed its mash bills and methods before his death in 2018. Hillrock was one of the first American “estate” distilleries, growing its own grain and distilling, aging and bottling everything on one farm.

Hillrock grows its grain on the estate, malts its own barley on a traditional malting floor and distills in a copper pot still. Its Solera Aged Bourbon, begun in October 2012, is described as the first solera-aged bourbon in America. A solera, borrowed from sherry making, is a tiered set of casks: whiskey is drawn from the oldest barrels and topped up with younger spirit, so no barrel is ever emptied. Hillrock’s solera combines its estate bourbon with mature “seed” bourbon and ages it in 20-year-old Oloroso sherry casks. The bourbon is a high-rye style, with roughly 37% rye in the mash, and is bottled at 92.6 proof.
facts: High-rye bourbon, about 37% rye (Port-cask edition lists 63% corn / 37% rye)
Copper pot still; estate-grown grain, floor-malted barley
